Question
========

Given the list `l <- list(a = 1, b = 2, c = 3)`, which statement correctly describes the difference between `l["a"]`
and `l[["a"]]`?

Answerlist
----------

* `l["a"]` returns a one-element list; `l[["a"]]` returns the numeric vector `1`.
* `l["a"]` and `l[["a"]]` always return exactly the same thing.
* `l["a"]` returns the numeric vector `1`; `l[["a"]]` returns a one-element list.
* `l["a"]` causes an error, since single brackets can't be used with names.
* `l[["a"]]` can select multiple named slots at once, while `l["a"]` cannot.

Solution
========

Single brackets (`[]`) always preserve the list "wrapper" around the result, even when selecting just one slot. So
`l["a"]` returns a one-element *list*. Double brackets (`[[]]`) reach inside and return the actual *contents* of a
single slot. So `l[["a"]]` returns the numeric vector `1`.
